data.name: Hadbar
data.gender_notes: Hadbar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'hadhara', meaning to be knowledgeable, wise and learned. The name Hadbar is an excellent choice for parents who wish to bestow a name with a noble and knowledgeable meaning upon their child. The name Hadbar carries the meaning “Wise, Knowledgeable” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Hadbar usually hope their child will grow to embody wise, knowledgeable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Encourages the development of wisdom and knowledge in the individual, helping them to grow into a well-rounded and enlightened person.
data.etymology: Hadbar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wise, Knowledgeable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hadbar total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hadbar signifies a person who is rich in knowledge and wisdom. It is a name that is deeply rooted in Islamic culture and tradition, where education and learning are highly valued attributes. A Hadbar is often seen as someone who is wise, intelligent and well-versed in various fields of knowledge.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Hadbar is a reminder of the importance of knowledge and wisdom in the Islamic faith. It is a name that encourages the pursuit of knowledge and the acquisition of wisdom, which is believed to be a means of drawing closer to God. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) once said, "The acquisition of knowledge is a duty on every Muslim." (Bukhari and Muslim) A Hadbar, therefore, is not only a knowledgeable and wise individual, but also a humble servant of God, always striving to increase his or her knowledge and deepen his or her connection with the Divine.
